title: Reproducing the coding-agreement audit (Cohen's kappa)
summary: Recompute the kappa figures published in the residual audit from the committed label sample, under four specifications, and compare each with the published value.
research_question: Does the upstream WATER / NOT_WATER filter agree well enough with an independent coder to support the jurimetric analysis, and can the published agreement figures be recomputed?
status_rationale: All four published point estimates (kappa, agreement, n) and the baseline per-category counts are recomputed within rounding. The bootstrap confidence intervals could not be reproduced exactly: the two published intervals disagree and neither seed nor row order is documented. Methodological fidelity to the original calculator is cross-checked, but no independent human review has happened.

validation_rules.description: Dataset checksum matches, labels belong to the allowed set, the runner executes.
Point estimates equal published values within their rounding precision.
Metrics equal an independent Python implementation.
The kappa formula equals the function in the original validation/kappa_calculator.py on the same labels.

limitations: The second coder is an LLM operating under written rules. This is a reproducibility audit of the regex filter, not human inter-coder reliability.
The calibration rule (0.832) was defined after the disagreements were seen on the same 91 decisions, so it is an in-sample figure.
The rule is applied to all Brazilian decisions where coder 1 said UNCERTAIN, because the dataset has no per-case topic flag. This reproduces the published figure.
Only 71 Dutch and 20 Brazilian decisions are sampled. Nothing is known about Canada.
Case identifiers are replaced by hashes in the public dataset; matching rows to the original decisions needs the researcher's private files.
unresolved: Bootstrap interval endpoints: kappa_results.json says [0.4441, 0.6908]; RESIDUAL_AUDIT.md says [0.436, 0.695]; re-running the original algorithm on the committed file order gives about [0.439, 0.692]. The origin of the differences is not documented.
README.md headlines kappa 0.832, but the committed kappa_results.json holds only the 0.568 baseline. The 0.832 figure is reproducible here but its generating output file is not in the repository.
